title: feat: stream media uploads up to 400 MiB
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
{"body":"- Streams existing `POST /upload` FormData and raw requests to R2 up to 400 MiB without changing client requests.
- Keeps base64 JSON uploads at 100 MiB to preserve Worker memory limits.
- Preserves custom IDs, tags, MIME defaults, gallery behavior, and 409 retries; adds integration coverage.
- Updates media upload limits in the source docs.

Verified: 55 media integration tests pass. A disposable Worker on the Enterprise `pollinations.ai` zone accepted a 400 MiB FormData upload; HEAD reported 419,430,400 bytes. A 110 MiB upload downloaded byte for byte correctly. The private staging Worker is deployed as version `4b861bd0-ea96-4e07-a641-2f7d7335122c`. The test Worker and objects were removed.

Chat conversation media still has a separate 20 MiB cap (#15889).

Addresses #11390"}

gist.headline: Bigger files, same upload door
gist.blurb: The media upload path learns to carry 400 MiB files straight to storage. Same requests, bigger parcels; base64 JSON keeps its 100 MiB limit.
gist.summary: POST /upload streams existing FormData and raw requests to R2 up to 400 MiB without client changes, while base64 JSON uploads retain their 100 MiB limit.
gist.impact: Apps can send media files up to 400 MiB through the existing FormData or raw upload flow, with custom IDs, tags, MIME defaults, gallery behavior, and 409 retries preserved; chat conversation media remains separately capped at 20 MiB.
gist.visual_concept: Show Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, helping a chunky 400 MiB file travel in pieces along a gentle stream into an R2 storage bucket. A smaller jar labeled 100 MiB represents the separate base64 JSON limit; code-plants and flowers make the storage shed feel like part of the garden.
